Company description:
This is the Volvo Group Graduate Program
 The 15-month Graduate Program combines 50% time in your home department with 50% dedicated program activities, giving you broad exposure across Volvo Group. Through local and international rotations, short-term assignments and targeted training in areas such as operations, engineering and purchasing, you will build a strong understanding of our business, brands and strategy.
 Job description:Your future teamWelcome to Systems Technology, part of Strategic Product Planning within Volvo Trucks Technology Industrial Division (TTI). We guide the system choices behind tomorrow's Volvo Group offers, from electrification and fuel-cell solutions via conventional powertrains to ADAS and electrical architecture. If you want your expertise to shape the next generation of sustainable transport, this is your chance to make that impact.
 How you’ll contributeYou will support the development of competitive sustainable and profitable future Volvo Group offers by connecting customer and business needs with technology systems and platform choices. This role contributes to strategic product plans, decision material and early-phase investigations and pre-studies, helping the organization make fact-based priorities across brands, applications and technology domains. 
 Key responsibilities
  Contribute to system product plans by analyzing customer needs, market and industry trends, regulations, competitors, technology maturity and business implications.
 Support strategic investigations and pre-studies; structure alternatives, dependencies, risks and trade-offs and prepare clear recommendations and decision material.
 Translate business and customer needs into product prerequisites, targets and planning input in collaboration with brands, engineering, portfolio functions and other stakeholders.
 Help identify Group synergies and platform opportunities while balancing common solutions with the needs of different brands, regions and applications.
 Build and share domain knowledge and a broad, T-shaped understanding of the complete vehicle, customer business and Volvo Group value chain.
 Communicate insights and plans in a simple, visual and compelling way and contribute to continuous improvement of product planning methods and ways of working.
  
Who are you?Your education and technical skills provide an important foundation, but what sets someone apart is the drive to make a meaningful difference. This role calls for high aspirations, energy, initiative, and ownership in turning ideas into results. It offers significant responsibility and the opportunity to influence decisions, shaping tomorrow’s transport solutions. No one needs to arrive with all the answers, but curiosity, a willingness to ask challenging questions and a commitment to making an exceptional contribution are essential.A transformation-oriented, collaborative mindset and a desire to understand the business is key. Success in this role means thriving in dynamic environments, embracing new challenges and ambiguity, and taking an active role in personal development. Strong analytical skills help move tasks forward, while fresh perspectives and innovative ideas strengthen the team. You enjoy building relationships and leveraging a global network help create impact across teams and functions. Sharing knowledge, exchanging insights, and supporting others’ development also contribute to a culture of continuous learning.Additionally, systems thinking comes naturally to you, along with the ability to connect technology choices to customer, product and business outcomes. Scenario work and business-case assessment are part of your toolkit and you know how to structure complex questions, compare alternatives and prepare fact-based recommendations.
 To qualify for the Graduate program, you:
  Have completed a master’s degree prior to the start of the program but not more than three years ago
 Relevant education within automotive, mechanical, electrical/electronic, energy systems, industrial engineering, innovation management or a related specialization combining technology and business
 Should not have more than three years' full-time relevant working experience in the field prior to starting, excluding part-time work during studies
 You are fluent in English, both written and verbal
 Valid work or study permit for Sweden if not a citizen
 You are willing to travel and participate in international short-term assignments
  
What’s in it for you?Our Volvo Group Graduate Program starts in August 2027 and you will be offered a permanent position at TTI – Strategic Product Planning department, with placement in Gothenburg, Sweden.These are some of the benefits of joining our program:
  An opportunity to work with the latest technology.
 An exciting and global working environment with experienced colleagues.
 Possibility to gain international experience through a short-term assignment abroad.
 A competitive salary and a permanent position from day one.
 Various workshops and seminars designed to help you grow into your future career at Volvo Group.
 The possibility to shape your own career with endless career opportunities.
  
The application processThe journey begins! An email confirmation will be sent when you submit your application. After this, it is still possible to update your personal profile by logging into your account. The hiring team will review your application together with the hiring manager. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted with information about the following steps.Last day to apply: 22nd of November 2026As part of the recruitment process, a background check as well as alcohol and drug testing may be conducted. You will be informed if applicable.

We are seeking an experienced System Integration HW & SW Test Engineer to qualify Building Management System (BMS) products and solutions, with a particular focus on system-level testing.The role combines hands-on hardware and software testing with the design and development of physical system test environments. The successful candidate will build representative BMS test systems, integrate hardware and software components, develop structured test suites, and execute system-level qualification testing.The engineer will work closely with software development, hardware development, system engineering, product management, and certification specialists to identify issues early and ensure that products meet functional, system, and certification requirements.The role will initially have a strong focus on establishing the test environment and performing hands-on testing.
  Key Responsibilities
 · Design, build, configure, and maintain physical system integration test environments for BMS products and solutions.
 · Integrate hardware, software, controllers, networks, field devices, and other required system components into representative test configurations.
 · Perform HW/SW system integration testing to verify functionality, interoperability, stability, and expected system behavior.
 · Develop and maintain structured system-level test plans, test cases, and reusable test suites.
 · Reproduce, analyze, document, and communicate defects discovered during system testing.
 · Work closely with software and hardware development teams to support root-cause investigation and verification of corrections.
 · Maintain test configurations and ensure that test setups are repeatable and representative of intended product configurations.
 · Document test results and provide clear evidence of system behavior and compliance.
 · Identify opportunities for test automation and develop test cases with automation in mind.
 · Automate suitable system tests directly or collaborate with software developers and test automation engineers to implement automated testing.
 · Contribute to continuous improvement of system integration, qualification, and certification processes.
 · Support formal certification activities by providing tested configurations, test evidence, technical information, and engineering support.
  Required Qualifications
 · Experience in system testing, system integration testing, or HW/SW integration testing.
 · Strong hands-on experience working with systems containing both hardware and software components.
 · Experience designing, setting up, configuring, and troubleshooting physical test systems.
 · Ability to translate system and certification requirements into structured and repeatable test cases.
 · Experience developing test plans, test cases, test procedures, and test reports.
 · Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills across hardware, software, communication, and system boundaries.
 · Ability to work independently and take ownership of complex system-level test activities.
 · Strong collaboration skills and ability to work effectively with hardware engineers, software developers, system engineers, and certification specialists.
 · Good English communication skills, both spoken and written, including the ability to clearly document test procedures, results, issues, and technical findings.
  
Preferred Qualifications
 · Experience with Building Management Systems (BMS), Building Automation Systems (BAS) or related building-control technologies.
 · Experience with automated system testing and test frameworks.
 · Experience preparing products or systems for third-party certification.
 · Experience working directly with certification organizations or certification laboratories.
 · Programming or scripting experience, for example Python or similar technologies used for test automation.
 · Experience testing communication networks, field buses, controllers, I/O, sensors, actuators, or other connected building-system components.
 · Experience with issue-tracking, requirements-management, test-management, and CI/CD tools.
 · Experience with Agile software and product-development processes.
 · Experience in the network technology environment BMS systems operate in.
  What Success Looks Like
 · A robust and representative physical system test environment is established and maintained.
 · HW/SW integration issues are identified early in the product-development lifecycle.
 · Product releases are systematically pre-tested against applicable UL 864 requirements before formal certification activities.
 · Certification-related test cases are documented, repeatable, and traceable.
 · Test suites evolve from individual manual tests into structured and reusable system test suites.
 · Suitable tests are progressively automated, reducing repetitive manual testing and improving regression-test coverage.
 · Test results and identified issues are clearly documented and effectively communicated to engineering teams.

jobs.description:
Department of Forest Ecology and Management  
Scientific background
Atmospheric aerosols are microscopic particles that influence weather and climate, contribute to biogeochemical cycling, and facilitate the dispersal of organisms. Aquatic systems can release aerosols into the atmosphere through processes such as bubble bursting, which have been studied extensively in oceans. However, whether and how these processes operate in streams remains poorly understood.
Streams differ from oceans in their hydrodynamics and water chemistry, potentially affecting how particles are captured by bubbles and potentially transferred to the atmosphere. Recent observations suggest that streams contain ice-nucleating particles that could become airborne, raising the possibility that boreal streams represent an overlooked source of atmospheric aerosols. The magnitude of these emissions, the mechanisms driving them, and the environmental factors controlling them remain largely unknown
About the position  
The postdoctoral researcher will investigate the hypothesis that streams emit aerosols to the atmosphere and identify the mechanisms and environmental conditions governing these emissions. A central task will be to develop a flux chamber to capture aerosols emitted from stream surfaces and quantify aerosol fluxes using online particle counters and air filtration for laboratory measurements of ice-nucleating particles. The chamber is planned to be deployed in both controlled experiments and field studies in natural boreal streams. The job also includes water sampling and measurements of physicochemical water and bubble properties.
The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to experimental design, data collection and analysis, manuscript preparation, scientific publication, and other forms of research communication. The position will be supervised by Associate Professor Marcus Klaus.
The successful candidate will be expected to work independently while collaborating closely with other members of the research team and external partners. The research environment will provide opportunities to develop scientific expertise, establish collaborations, and strengthen the candidate's professional development and academic career prospects.
Your profile
We are seeking a motivated and dedicated researcher with expertise at the interface of aquatic and atmospheric sciences and a strong interest in air–water exchange processes. Applicants must hold a PhD in atmospheric sciences, aquatic sciences, physics, environmental engineering, or a related discipline. 
The applicant must have demonstrated experience in measurements of aerosols, suspended particles and/or air-water mass exchange (particles or gases) and experience conducting laboratory and/or fieldwork in aquatic and/or atmospheric systems. A track record of scientific writing and publishing in peer-reviewed journals is also required, as are excellent written and spoken English skills.  
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:
Air filtration, aerosol sampling, and particle counting
Droplet freezing assays
Bubble and/or turbulence characterization
Programming and data analysis using tools such as R or MATLAB
Engineering, instrument development, or practical skills relevant to designing and constructing the flux chamber  

In addition to scientific qualifications, emphasis will be placed on personal suitability, including scientific curiosity, initiative, the ability to work independently, and a constructive and collaborative approach to teamwork. 
As postdoctoral appointments are career-developing positions for junior researchers, we are primarily looking for candidates with a doctoral degree that is three years old at most.

Excellent spoken and written English.

ML platforms and MLOps tooling, such as MLflow and experiment tracking. 
PyTorch, and model deployment or inference optimization, such as TensorRT. 
Workflow orchestration and ETL. We use Flyte, but experience with Airflow, Prefect, Dagster or similar is just as relevant. 
Kubernetes, cloud platforms and infrastructure as code.

Web application development. 
Medical imaging (DICOM, RT structures), healthcare technology or other regulated, safety-critical environments.

Bring the Future of Wind Propulsion Onboard

About Us
Wind helped us discover our planet, and now it can help us preserve it. Our vision is to provide wings for a shipping revolution, and we have two strong mother companies to back us up: Alfa Laval and Wallenius.
Would you like to contribute to this change, then join our fast-growing, highly competent and passionate team. AlfaWall Oceanbird AB is a 50/50 joint venture, owned by Alfa Laval and Wallenius but operated as an independent company. We are developing wing sail technology for the global shipping market and are now looking for an Installation Lead to join our team. Help us bring wind propulsion from shore to ship!
The role
As Oceanbird moves from a prototype stage into commercial customer delivery, successful installation is becoming one of our most important capabilities.
As Installation Lead, you will turn plans and technical solutions into safe, efficient and wellcoordinated installations at shipyards and onboard vessels. You will also be responsible for our demonstrator wing in Landskrona, coordinating its operation, maintenance and test readiness so that it provides the data needed for our continued development.

You will be part of the Project Management Office and work closely with our project managers. During installations, you will lead a cross-functional team of approximately 3–8 people, including electricians, service engineers, technical specialists and external contractors.
The Project Manager retains overall responsibility for the customer project, while you lead the dayto-day installation activities and safe execution at the shipyard, in harbor or at sea.

Your main responsibilities:
• Plan, prepare and lead installation and commissioning activities at shipyards/harbour and onboard vessels.
• Translate project and engineering requirements into practical installation plans, work sequences, resource needs and schedules.
• Coordinate the on-site installation team and act as Oceanbird’s operational interface with shipyards, vessel crews, customers and subcontractors.
• Lead the safe execution of installation work, ensuring that risk assessments, work permits, toolbox talks and agreed safety procedures are in place and followed.
• Monitor progress, quality and safety, resolve practical issues and escalate risks or decisions when required.
• Develop and maintain installation procedures, method statements, SOPs, checklists and installation manuals.
• Capture lessons learned and use them to improve future installations, documentation and ways of working.
• Coordinate the operation, maintenance, inspection and test readiness of the demonstrator wing and its supporting equipment in Landskrona.
• Plan activities together with the Landskrona team and work closely with our teams in Flemingsberg to incorporate experience from installations and testing into our continued development.

Who are you?
You are a practical and confident installation leader who can bring people from different disciplines together, create structure and maintain focus on safety and delivery—even when conditions change.
You are likely to have:
• Experience leading installations, commissioning, service or major maintenance involving complex mechanical or electromechanical equipment.

Classified by Alfa Laval as: Business
• Experience from commercial vessels and shipyards, ideally involving bulk carriers, tankers or similar vessel types.
• Experience from newbuild projects and working closely with shipyards in Asia is highly valuable.
• A relevant engineering qualification within mechanical, marine, electrical or a related technical field. This could be a vocational, college or bachelor-level qualification, or equivalent experience.
• A strong understanding of safe working practices in shipyard, industrial or onboard environments.
• Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams, contractors and external stakeholders.
• The ability to produce clear and practical technical documentation, including SOPs and installation manuals.
• Professional proficiency in English and the willingness to travel internationally and work onboard vessels.

You are safety-conscious, structured and calm under pressure. You communicate clearly across technical disciplines and cultures and are comfortable moving between planning, documentation and hands-on execution.

Location and travel
We are open to discussing the location for the right candidate, although proximity to either Flemingsberg or Landskrona is preferred.
Regular international travel and periods of work at shipyards and onboard vessels are an integral part of the role.

What we offer
At Oceanbird, you will help turn a bold vision into working technology at sea. You will see the direct result of your work as our wing sail technology moves from development and testing to installation onboard commercial vessels—and ultimately into operation at sea.
This is an opportunity to shape not only how our first commercial installations are delivered, but how Oceanbird will install wing sails around the world in the future. Working alongside highly skilled and passionate colleagues, you will influence our installation methods, safety standards and ways of working—and contribute directly to making wind a powerful part of cleaner shipping.

Join us in redefining the future of clean shipping.
Apply today and be part of a journey that truly makes a difference!

Would you like to play a key part in Toca Boca’s Data & Research engine? With over 60 million monthly active users and terabytes of daily data, as a Senior Data Scientist, you will play an integral role in understanding how kids and families engage with our play ecosystem, directly shaping fantastic, safe, and imaginative play experiences.

At Toca Boca, we don’t lock you into narrow corporate silos or endless maintenance tasks. As a Senior Data Scientist, you will enjoy broad end-to-end ownership across the entire product lifecycle—from exploratory data science, advanced modeling, and experimentation to product strategy and monetization dynamics.

You’ll join our Data & Analytics team while partnering seamlessly with our User Research team under a unified Insights banner. Together, we blend big data behavioral telemetry with qualitative player research, working closely with cross-functional game teams to unlock the full value of our play ecosystem.

What you’ll be doing

Uncover Deep Player Insights: Analyze complex player datasets to understand behavioral patterns, feature engagement, and retention drivers across our games, informing overall product and commerce strategy.
Apply Advanced Statistical Methods: Apply statistical models, regression analysis, predictive segmentation, and experimental methods (A/B testing) to optimize product performance at scale.
Bridge Quantitative & Qualitative Insights: Partner seamlessly with our User Research team under a unified Insights banner, connecting the "what" (big data trends) with the "why" (qualitative research) to deliver a 360-degree understanding of our players.

Broad Impact: You thrive with the freedom to influence multiple product areas—from core play loops and feature design to commerce and top-of-funnel engagement—without being pigeonholed.
Holistic Insights: You successfully bridge quantitative behavioral data with qualitative user research to create unified narratives that inspire game design.
Autonomy & Momentum: You help teams move quickly by surfacing key facts, reducing ambiguity, and solving open-ended problems that don't have predefined playbooks.

Is This You?

3+ years of experience (or equivalent senior-level impact) in user-focused Data Science or Advanced Product Analytics within Gaming, Mobile Apps, or Interactive Digital Products.
Empathy & Product Sense: Deep curiosity and intuition for player experience, engagement, and kids' digital environments.
SQL Mastery & Data Exploration: Outstanding SQL skills querying cloud data warehouses (experience with Google BigQuery and DBT is a huge plus).
Advanced DS Toolkit: Proficiency in Python (or R) for statistical modeling, machine learning, segmentation, and exploratory deep dives. Experience with BI tools like Tableau or Looker is a great plus!
Rigorous Statistical Foundation: Strong track record in experimentation lifecycle design, A/B test analysis, and hypothesis testing.
AI & Modern Workflows (Nice to have): Curiosity or Hands-on experience building, integrating, or utilizing AI/LLM tools within your data workflows or analytics stack.
Clear Storytelling & Autonomy: Skilled at translating complex quantitative and qualitative data into simple, compelling recommendations for non-technical partners. Thrives with high autonomy in fast-paced environments.

We celebrate the diversity and quirkiness of their world and give them the freedom to play in ways that only they can.

Good to know!

With offices in Stockholm and San Francisco, Toca Boca is owned by Spin Master Corp., a global children’s entertainment company that creates, designs and manufactures a diversified portfolio of innovative toys, games, products and entertainment properties.

Are you a highly capable finance professional who wants to build and manage the financial backbone of a rapidly growing deep-tech and medical technology company?
Ascilion is now recruiting a Financial Controller to the company. The position is full-time and based at our headquarters in Kista.
At Ascilion we are singularly focused on solving one of medicine’s big challenges: providing real-time access to molecular biomarkers. Ascilion’s proprietary, industry-leading microneedle technology enables quick, reliable, and painless access to molecular biomarkers.
Ascilion is entering a phase of significant international growth with substantial investor involvement, increasing reporting requirements, expanding operations, and likely future subsidiaries and / or international sales entities. We already work with strong external partners in bookkeeping and audits, but we now need an internal financial leader who owns the full picture and ensures the company operates at a world-class level financially and operationally.
The Financial Controller is a key leadership position responsible for the overall financial management of the company, ensuring the accuracy, integrity, and compliance of our financial reporting. Depending on profile and experience, the role may develop into a CFO position and become part of the senior management team with responsibility for strategic financial planning and board-level reporting. This is an excellent opportunity for you to join a dedicated and highly competent team and a growing company with an exciting journey ahead. If this sounds interesting to you, please contact us using the details below!
We will interview candidates continuously for the position and welcome your application today.
Responsibilities
As our Financial Controller, you will drive the company’s financial success by ensuring reporting accuracy, robust compliance, and strategic control over day-to-day financial operations. You will report directly to the CEO.
Your main responsibilities will be to:

Own and manage the company’s financial operations and reporting structure

Ensure high-quality financial reporting towards investors, board, auditors, and authorities

Prepare board material, financial presentations, forecasts, and KPI reporting

Coordinate and manage relationships with bookkeeping firms, auditors, banks, investors, and external financial partners

Develop and improve internal financial processes, controls, and reporting systems

Support international expansion including subsidiaries, sales offices, and cross-border financial structures

Drive budgeting, liquidity planning, cash flow management, and long-term financial planning

Ensure audit readiness, regulatory compliance, and professional financial governance

Support operational scaling of the company together with management and technical leadership

Potentially take responsibility for HR administration, contracts, insurance, and internal operational processes depending on profile and interest

Your Profile
Key qualifications for the position include:

Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or Economics.

Several years of experience in accounting, with a strong focus on financial reporting, accounting, controlling, and compliance

Experience working with investors, boards, auditors, and external financial stakeholders

Strong understanding of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and corporate governance

A deep understanding of Swedish GAAP. Direct experience with US GAAP or IFRS is a competitive advantage

Experience from scaling companies, international operations, startups, medtech, deep-tech, or manufacturing environments is highly valuable

Experience with subsidiaries, international reporting structures, or US operations is a strong plus

Fluency in Swedish and English

We are looking for a structured, reliable, and highly detailed-oriented professional who enjoys taking ownership and creating order and clarity in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. As a person, you are analytical, strategic, pragmatic and execution-focused, with a strong ability to work with both details and the bigger picture. You have strong communication and collaboration skills, and you are comfortable operating close to both management and technical teams and presenting financial information clearly to both investors and engineers. Importantly, you thrive in an ambitious, high-performance environment and want to help build a globally significant company, not just manage spreadsheets
At Ascilion, you will have the opportunity to make an impact not only in your own area of responsibility, but also on the development of the company as a whole.
About Ascilion
Ascilion was founded in 2012 with a mission to solve the problem of sampling dermal interstitial fluid in an efficient and pain-free way. A team of engineers with deep experience in MEMS technology and microfluidics took on the challenge of solving what turned out to be a very complex problem.
We exist to bridge the worlds of precision engineering and biomarker science, creating innovative microneedle technologies that make dISF accessible, reliable, and painless; empowering researchers, clinicians, and companies to unlock the full potential of health monitoring and diagnostics.
We are currently in a very exciting expansion phase where we grow all aspects of the organization from R&D to sales. Our customer base is increasing with numerous close collaborations in Europe, the US, and Asia. Come, join our journey!

By 2030, our ambition is to produce 5 million tonnes of green steel annually in our fully integrated, digitized, and sustainable plant in Boden, Northern Sweden - currently under construction.
